text: An orderBy() clause also filters for the existence of the field: documents that don't have it are left out of the results.
author: Firebase

text: Deleting a document doesn't delete its subcollections. They stay readable at their full path.
author: Firebase

text: A document can hold at most 1 MiB of data, field names included.
author: Firebase

text: Subcollections can nest up to 100 levels deep.
author: Firebase

text: Document IDs can't be . or .., and can't look like __name__: double underscores at both ends are reserved.
author: Firebase

text: The in, not-in and array-contains-any operators take up to 30 values.
author: Firebase

text: A query can have only one array-contains clause.
author: Firebase

text: != and not-in skip documents where the field doesn't exist at all.
author: Firebase

text: A query takes time in proportion to the size of its result, not the size of the collection.
author: Firebase

text: In a transaction, every read must come before the first write.
author: Firebase

text: Transactions fail when the client is offline. Batched writes don't need a connection to be queued.
author: Firebase

text: Monotonically increasing document IDs, like timestamps, create hotspots. Prefer auto-generated IDs.
author: Firebase
